clue.text: Service providing gas pressure?

parts.note: air is the mixture of gases we breathe
force is a synonym for pressure, as in applying force

explanation.surface: A question about which branch of the forces supplies gas under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' is one of the armed services, not a utility, despite the gas talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The air force is one of the three armed services alongside army and navy.

clue.text: A portion for each person

parts.note: a piece is a portion of something

explanation.surface: Sharing out a slice for every diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece is an adverb meaning to or for each one.

clue.text: Administration putting soldier in wrong corps

indicators.note: in signals that the soldier is placed inside the corps

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A government that posts a soldier to the wrong unit.
explanation.walkthrough: GI, an American soldier, ends up in a British corps, which is why it is the wrong corps; 'wrong' adds colour and supplies nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a system of government or management.

clue.text: Old blackbird found in house loft

indicators.note: found in means the letters are sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An old bird discovered nesting up under the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouzel or ousel is an old and poetic name for the common blackbird.

clue.text: Belief about a teamleader being made

indicators.note: about tells us the belief is wrapped round what follows

parts.note: a creed is a set of beliefs
the leader of team is its first letter

explanation.surface: A faith growing up around a captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Created means brought into existence, past participle of create.

clue.text: Shivering like fish

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
the hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone trembling the way a fish quivers on the slab.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shaking or trembling is to be shivering; the a- prefix makes an old adjective as in afloat.

clue.text: The patience of the Americans

parts.note: the card game the British call patience goes by another name in the United States

explanation.definitionFit: Americans use this name for the one-player card game patience.

clue.text: Minor planet supplying a type of hormone

parts.note: steroids are a class of hormones such as testosterone

explanation.surface: A small planet that is a source of hormones.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun.

clue.text: Jeopardise the finish with wrath

parts.note: an end is a finish
anger is wrath

explanation.surface: Putting the conclusion at risk through fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeopardise is to put at risk or in peril.

clue.text: End gets concoction eaten

indicators.note: a concoction mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters of END GETS as written, plus the I the setter's slip left out, form the anagram pool

explanation.surface: The final part of a recipe gets eaten once the mixture is made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' stirs the fodder, but END GETS gives only seven letters; the answer also needs an I, which the clue as printed never supplies, so a word such as 'I' appears to have dropped out.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been swallowed and taken into the body has been consumed.

clue.text: Abused as a roof may be

definitions.meaning: harshly criticised, as a play is by reviewers
a roof can be covered with slates

explanation.definitionFit: To slate is British slang for to criticise severely, and roofs are commonly tiled with slate.

clue.text: Thought I'd take half of each

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of the word each

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they will take a half share of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a notion that comes to mind.

clue.text: Learner entered into contest outside and finished

indicators.note: outside tells us the first piece sits around the learner letter

parts.note: to have entered into a contest is to have competed
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A learner driver took part in a competition held outdoors and finished it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like the place the contest was held, but it puts COMPETED around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completed is done or brought to an end.

clue.text: I turn round in Italian city

indicators.note: turning round signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller turns around when reaching a city in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is the major city of Piedmont in northern Italy.

clue.text: Hurried with odds to editor

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race

explanation.surface: Someone rushed off to show a newspaper editor some betting odds.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is the bookmakers' odds at the off of a British horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Sped is the past tense of speed, meaning rushed.

clue.text: Simple argument produced by accuser

parts.note: plain means simple
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A straightforward quarrel brought by someone making a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff brings a case against someone in a court of law.

clue.text: A misdemeanour in the east could be stupid

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing or misdeed
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Committing a petty offence in the Orient might be foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means silly or foolish, literally like an ass.

clue.text: Heretic I work upon afterwards

parts.note: to do is to work or perform
later means afterwards

explanation.surface: An unbeliever saying they will deal with something later.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships false gods, so is a heretic to orthodox religion.

clue.text: Is mother upset by heat line

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A mother thrown out by being struck in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotherm is a line on a map joining places of equal temperature.

clue.text: Hopelessness of some French couple

parts.note: des is French for some, the plural partitive article
a pair is a couple of things

explanation.surface: A French pair feeling utterly without hope.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the complete loss of hope.

clue.text: Soldiers accept it as a ceremonial form

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the soldiers surround the word it

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Troops taking something on as a formal ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a ceremony performed according to a set form.

clue.text: Bump into huntsmen

definitions.meaning: a gathering of riders and hounds before a fox hunt

explanation.definitionFit: To come across someone is to encounter them, and the assembly of a fox hunt is called a meet.

clue.text: Young lady I take on in embassy

parts.note: a miss is a young woman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman being taken on at a diplomatic post.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission is a diplomatic body sent abroad, as an embassy is.

clue.text: Using maximum effort when the innings is finished

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a side's innings ends when ten batsmen are dismissed

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an innings is a team's turn to bat, which ends once ten of the eleven batsmen are out.
explanation.definitionFit: Total effort is described as all-out, and in cricket a team bowled out has lost all its wickets.

clue.text: Stick notice in this place

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement or notice
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Posting a notice on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or stay fixed to something.

clue.text: The French can compose this language

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
a tin is a can, in British usage

explanation.surface: A French tin might hold the makings of a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the classical tongue of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Tell about fool going to editor with ornamental fringe

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the word tell surrounds the fool

parts.note: taken as written
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Telling tales about a fool who goes to the editor wearing a fringed garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes TELL wrap round the fool rather than meaning concerning; 'with ornamental fringe' is an adjectival definition, fair because a tasselled garment is one trimmed with a fringe of tassels.
explanation.definitionFit: Tassels are hanging tufts of threads used as decorative trimming.

clue.text: Destroy as before outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for before goes round the other piece

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Wrecking things just as before, in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or obliterate.

clue.text: Knot and fasten appendage to neckware

parts.note: a tie is a knot, as in tying a knot
to pin something is to fasten it

explanation.surface: Instructions to knot and secure something worn at the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative pin clips a necktie to the shirt front.

clue.text: Protective clothing to fasten in front

parts.note: to pin is to fasten
afore is an old word for before or in front

explanation.surface: An apron or overall that ties up at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless apron-like garment worn to keep clothes clean.

clue.text: Divide into branches if army disintegrates

indicators.note: something disintegrating breaks up, so these letters fall apart and regroup

explanation.surface: An army breaking up splits into separate units.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramify is to spread out by forking, like the limbs of a tree.

clue.text: Fluster United Nations' bench

parts.note: UN is the abbreviation for United Nations
a settle is a wooden bench with a high back

explanation.surface: Unsettling the delegates by meddling with the United Nations seating.
explanation.walkthrough: A settle is a high-backed wooden bench, often found in old English pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluster someone is to disturb their composure.
